title: Read-only refusal explainer: drift guard is one-way, and quoted `>&` or `|&` lines are misattributed (background vs redirection)
outcome:
Two message-accuracy gaps in src/claude_read_only_refusal.rs. Neither changes any allow or deny decision.

(1) Drift. CLAUDE_READ_ONLY_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS and CLAUDE_OPTION_CHECKED_BASH_COMMANDS are tested against the checker in one direction only. claude_git_tokens_are_read_only and claude_bash_tokens_are_read_only still dispatch on literals, so a subcommand or head added to the checker but not to the const goes undetected. The refusal would then say "`git X` is not one of the read-only commands" for a command the gate allows with other arguments.
Fix: drive the dispatch from the consts, for example with an early contains check, so a new arm cannot exist without its list entry.

(2) Background versus redirection. When the background-separator scan fires, the explainer looks for `>&`, `<&` or `&>` anywhere in the raw line, quotes included.
- `echo '2>&1' & git status` is named a redirection, although the checker applied the background rule to the unquoted `&`.
- `git log |& head` is named a background `&`, although `|&` is a stderr pipe.
Fix: classify the actual unquoted ampersand the scanner found, and treat `|&` as redirection. Add regression rows.
acceptance: A git subcommand or option-checked head the checker allows cannot be missing from the refusal's lists without a test failing.
A line whose only real `&` is a background separator, with redirection-like text inside quotes, is named as background; `|&` is named as redirection; tests cover both.
The full five-stage gate passes on the reviewed tree, and the review pair has no outstanding Medium or higher.
